_readme: Single source of truth for the worker's wire vocabulary: the notification-type tokens the platform persists inside notification envelopes (the Go agent package's NotificationType* constants and the browser's NOTIFICATION_TYPE are generated from this file), the notification-thread wrapper discriminator, the one Codex rateLimitReachedType that lifts on a timer, and the model sentinels. workerAuthoredNotificationTypes lists the types the WORKER is the sole writer of -- the browser keeps a standalone-row set from it, and a type moves between the two regimes by editing this file, not by editing a per-side list. Adding a notification type is: one entry here, task generate, and both sides' dispatch switches compile against it. GoalUpdated/GoalCleared are worker-authored on purpose: five providers report a session goal in five different wire shapes, and persisting each verbatim would put every provider's goal parsing in that provider's renderer. The worker normalizes once and writes a neutral row, so the browser has ONE goal renderer. goalStatusTokens and goalTransitions are the session goal's two payload vocabularies. The worker writes both inside the goal_updated notification -- goal_status is the neutral status the row stores, goal_transition is what the change DID -- and notificationRenderers reads both to build the transcript line. Both were hand-written on the two sides before this contract existed, and the status tokens are ALSO the SQL CHECK list on agents.goal_status, which the generator cannot emit; keep that third spelling in step by hand. goal_transition is a separate vocabulary from the status because several different changes land on one status: a resume and a first set both end `active`, and only the applier, which holds the row from before the write, can tell them apart. Every token here has a producer in goalTransitionKind; a token nothing writes is a label the browser can never render, so add one only with the branch that emits it.
